doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: Learning flute and clarinet for folk and Dixieland gigs
summary: He learned flute for London folk clubs and clarinet for Dixieland, moving between scenes in one day.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: And then I’m going to guess that down the road you crossed paths again with some of these same musicians in a different context?

Oh always, yes. I mean very early on I, as a sax player, I decided that it’d be a good idea to learn to play the flute and clarinet, not because I wanted to be in a big band or anything like that, but if I played the flute I could go to a folk club and play with the up-and- coming Mick Drakes and John Martins and people like that who populated the London folk scene. And if I played the clarinet I could do Dixieland gigs, which I started doing though it was very schizophrenic you know. One day I’d be on the blues scene or even the same day, then I’d go to a folk club and then I’d do a Dixieland gig later on. But I was voracious. I loved music. Music was everywhere.
You were getting on-the-job training for your composing and your arranging.
Like it all was going into your head.
